# square-wave-generator

<!-- Generated by tools/build-user-docs.py; edit tools/sketch-guides.json. -->

**Level:** Signals / serial. No AI subscription or API key is needed.

[Start here](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/getting-started.html) · [Website instructions](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/sketches.html#square-wave-generator) · [All sketches](../README.md)

## What you should see

Channel 1 drives D13 at 1 Hz and 50% duty immediately; the built-in LED mirrors it. The upper matrix half shows its waveform.

## What you need

Disconnect attached circuits before uploading: D13 is driven at startup. No components are needed to see the built-in LED demo. For measurements, use a compatible oscilloscope or logic analyzer with common GND. Never connect an output to another output.

Install Arduino_RouterBridge with Library Manager. The UNO Q core supplies the board-specific headers.

## Upload this sketch

1. Complete the getting-started guide once to install the UNO Q core and libraries.
2. In Arduino IDE, open square-wave-generator/square-wave-generator.ino. Select Arduino UNO Q and its port.
3. Click Verify, then Upload. Uploading replaces the running microcontroller sketch.

Or, in the **UNO Q Linux terminal**, from the repository root:

```bash
python3 flash square-wave-generator
```

Read the replacement prompt and enter `y` to compile and upload. To check compilation without uploading:

```bash
python3 flash square-wave-generator --compile-only
```

The helper uploads locally on the board. For a computer-side IDE or network CLI upload, follow the getting-started guide.

## Try it

With external circuits disconnected, send OUT 1 D9 2 50, then STATUS. Channel 1 moves to D9 at 2 Hz. Send OFF 1 to drive it LOW.

## Send commands

Follow [the serial monitor setup](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/getting-started.html#serial): 115200 baud, newline ending, one command per line. Values in angle brackets describe what to enter; do not type the brackets. A slash separates alternatives.

- `OUT <1|2> <D2-D13> <0.1-1000> <1-99>` — channel, pin, frequency in Hz, duty in percent
- `OFF <1|2>` — stop the channel and drive its pin LOW
- `SWEEP <channel> <start Hz> <end Hz> <seconds>` — logarithmic sweep; 0.1–1000 Hz and 0.1–3600 seconds; configure OUT first
- `STATUS` — report both channels
- `HELP` — list commands

Serial input still needs end-to-end verification. Settings are held in memory and reset when the sketch restarts.

## Limits and tips

This uses software timing, not a precision hardware signal source. High frequencies and extreme duty cycles can have substantial jitter. The matrix samples slowly and cannot show a high-frequency waveform accurately.

## If it does not work

Compare the result with the expected behavior above, then follow [troubleshooting](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/getting-started.html#troubleshooting). Save your edits before downloading or uploading another version.

The repository records compilation with UNO Q core 0.56.0 on the original board. Typed serial input and most visual behavior still need hardware verification. These instructions describe the source code, not a new hardware test.

[Read the source](square-wave-generator.ino) for the implementation and its original compile/upload commands.
